title: Goblin Slayer: Brand New Day
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A two-volume collection of side stories set around Goblin Slayer, a man single-mindedly devoted to killing goblins. Chapters follow people who cross his path, such as a rookie warrior and an apprentice cleric seeking his advice and a tavern waitress, alongside the goblins in their nest.
life_message: It holds up grim competence and protecting ordinary people from monsters, with everyday life going on around the danger.

content.note: Goblin slaughter and gore; Yen Press rates it 18+ M (AniList Gore; MU Blood and Gore, Violence; MangaDex Gore).
Yen Press shelves it as Horror; MangaDex Tragedy tag; goblin nests as threat.
MU lists Rape, Nudity and Borderline H; MangaDex lists Sexual Violence. Databases only, so capped (to verify; possibly understated).
Tavern setting; adult drinking likely (to verify).
Goblin Slayer's obsessive focus; not detailed in sources (to verify).
Spin-off of a larger light-novel franchise.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Threats are answered personally by Goblin Slayer's blade rather than by any authority (Yen Press blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Adventurers act independently in a remote town; the guild is in the background (to verify).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Protection extends to the whole town and newcomers, not just kin.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Rookies seek a veteran's advice; mentoring without strict rank (Yen Press blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Clerics and gods exist in the setting alongside practical method (to verify).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival against goblins and daily subsistence dominate.

folkways.japan: Mentoring of rookies by a veteran echoes Japanese senpai-kohai norms; the fantasy setting itself draws on Western role-playing games.

delivery.evidence: Episodic side stories with no stated thesis (Yen Press and MU summaries); sources say nothing on delivery (to verify).
delivery.note: The series presents its world without arguing for a view; goblins are threats rather than holders of a position.

winners_losers: Goblin Slayer and the townspeople win; the goblins are given no sympathy.
